Apples Dipped in Honey

Served at: Rosh Hashanah (Jewish New Year)

Serves 4-6Prep 10 min

Apples dipped in honey are a central and beloved tradition during Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year. This simple yet profound dish symbolizes our heartfelt wishes for a sweet, fruitful, and blessed year ahead, making it the first food eaten after the holiday blessings.

Ingredients

  • 4-6 medium crisp apples (such as Honeycrisp, Gala, Fuji, or Granny Smith)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) good quality honey (local or wildflower preferred)

Method

  1. Gently wash and dry all the apples thoroughly.
  2. Carefully core the apples, if desired, or leave them whole for slicing.
  3. Slice each apple into 6-8 wedges or rounds, removing any seeds.
  4. Arrange the apple slices attractively on a serving platter or individual plates.
  5. Pour the honey into a small, elegant serving bowl or a honey pot.
  6. Place the bowl of honey alongside the apple slices, ready for dipping.
  7. Before eating, recite the traditional blessing for fruit and the blessing for a sweet new year.

Tips

  • For an extra touch, sprinkle a tiny pinch of ground cinnamon or a few pomegranate seeds over the honey just before serving.
  • Offer a variety of apple types for different flavor profiles and textures.
  • Ensure the honey is at room temperature for easy dipping; if it's too thick, gently warm it slightly in a microwave or a warm water bath.
